events.objective: Establish the true symptom onset time and blast radius around 2026-06-01 14:30-16:59Z. Determine exactly when payment-service error rate began rising (verify the reported ~15 min after release), what the dominant error signatures/status codes are (especially ledger write failures), and whether ledger-service or any other service shows elevated errors/latency in the same window. Report per-service error/latency trends and any resource saturation signals (DB connections, CPU, disk) on payment-service and ledger-service.

Enumerate all changes (deployments and config changes) across ALL services between 2026-06-01 13:00Z and 16:00Z, not just payment-service. Specifically capture payment-service v6.0.0 timing, any ledger-service deploys/config/migrations, schema or entry-type changes, and feature flags. Also map service dependencies for payment-service and ledger-service (shared components, datastore) and search historical incidents for prior ledger write / new-entry-type failures to identify precedents.

Correlate the onset time from task a with the change timestamps from task b: for each candidate change, compute whether error onset lag matches, and test whether errors are confined to the new mandate-flow path (new ledger entry type) versus all ledger writes. Specifically check whether ledger write failures occur for non-mandate/legacy entry types too, which would rule out the release-introduced type as the sole cause.

events.statement: Exactly one deployment occurred across all services between 2026-06-01T13:00Z and 16:00Z: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203), deployed 14:46:00Z by p.nair, summarised 'New UPI mandate flow', changes 'mandate create/approve endpoints' and 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD'; status 'rolled_back' at 15:12:00Z.

Rollback of dep-6203 occurred at 15:12:00Z, i.e. 26 minutes after deploy; the incident was reported at 15:10:00Z, so the rollback began ~2 minutes after the report and before the reported 'current time' of 16:59:00Z.
No config changes (flags, toggles, env/app config, schema-config entries) were recorded for any service in 2026-06-01T13:00Z–16:00Z; result was empty with count 0, not truncated.

There is no service named 'ledger-service' in the inventory; the ledger is the shared Postgres datastore 'ledger-db' (owner platform, shared=true). Known services list contains 'ledger-db' but no ledger-service.

ledger-db is a shared datastore written by four services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all hold 'db' edges into ledger-db, so write failures on the new MANDATE_HOLD path can affect and be affected by neighbours through this shared component.

payment-service's other dependency edges are: ledger-db (db), bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), kafka (queue-produce, shared), and inbound api-gateway -> payment-service (http). Precedent leads from history involving ledger-db are write-failure/disk-full (HIST-114, 'no space left on device','write failures') and failover-induced connection refusals (HIST-102) — leads only, different root causes.

events.description: Could not verify whether any ledger-db migration / schema change (e.g. adding the MANDATE_HOLD entry type to a DB enum/check constraint) was applied: get_config_changes returned an empty set for all windows queried, and the two follow-up historical-incident searches for entry-type/enum-write and payment-release precedents were not executed.

search_historical_incidents calls for 'enum constraint violation new transaction type write rejected' and 'payment-service release rollback error rate spike' returned budget_exhausted and were never run; only 1 of 3 planned precedent searches (tc-005, 5 results) completed.

events.answer: The only change in the 13:00–16:00Z window across all services was the payment-service v6.0.0 deploy (dep-6203) at 14:46:00Z, which introduced the MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type and was rolled back at 15:12:00Z. There is no "ledger-service": the ledger is a shared Postgres datastore (ledger-db) used by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service, so a new entry type persisted by payment-service lands in a shared component. No config/flag changes were reported in that window.

events.statement: payment-service error_rate is flat at ~0.2-0.3% from 14:00Z through the 14:54Z bucket (last pre-onset bucket avg 0.19, max 0.28), then jumps to avg 61.9 / max 66.98 in the 15:00:00Z bucket and stays elevated at ~60-64% for the rest of the window (last bucket 16:54Z avg 61.26). The 6-min buckets place onset between 14:54Z and 15:00Z, i.e. ~15:00Z, which is ~2.5h, not the reported ~15 min after release.

ALL 354 ERROR-level payment-service log lines in 14:00-16:59Z carry a single signature: 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device (payment <n>)'. First match is 2026-06-01T15:00:26Z and last 15:57:54Z-ish, tightly aligned with the metric onset at 15:00Z.

ledger-db (the datastore behind ledger writes; there is no service named 'ledger-service') emits 292 ERROR log lines starting 2026-06-01T15:01:01Z, dominated by disk-space signatures: 'PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.<n>": No space left on device' (153) and 'could not extend file "base/<n>/<n>": No space left on device' (139). This is the source matching payment-service's 'could not extend file' errors and is ~35s later than the first payment error.

payment-service latency_p99_ms shows NO degradation: pre-onset 14:00-14:54Z is ~316-333ms and post-onset 15:00-16:54Z stays in the same band (~309-330ms avg, max 348.32). So the failure is a hard write error, not a latency/saturation symptom.

payment-service has NO application-level resource saturation: db_pool_in_use stays ~7.1-8.9 connections across the whole window (15:00Z avg 7.99) and cpu_pct stays ~27-33% (15:00Z avg 30.26, max 32.99) both before and after onset.

ledger-db exposes disk metrics (available_metrics include 'disk_used_pct' and 'slow_queries_per_min') and does NOT expose an 'error_rate' metric; a disk-usage timeline for ledger-db was not retrieved before budget ran out, so the disk-fill onset is inferred from log first-seen times only.

events.answer: True onset is ~2026-06-01T15:00Z (between the 14:54Z and 15:00Z buckets), NOT 15 min after release as reported. payment-service error_rate jumps from ~0.2% to ~62% at 15:00Z with a single dominant signature — 'ledger write failed: ... could not extend file: No space left on device' (354/354 errors, first at 15:00:26Z). The backing datastore ledger-db (no service named 'ledger-service') shows the matching root signal: 292 errors from 15:01:01Z, including 153 'PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp...": No space left on device' and 139 'could not extend file "base/...": No space left on device' — i.e. disk full, not application saturation. payment-service latency (~320ms) and resources (db_pool_in_use ~8, cpu ~30%) are normal throughout, ruling out CPU/pool saturation on the service side.

events.statement: Error onset is at 15:00Z: payment-service error_rate is flat 0.17-0.29% through the 14:57Z bucket (14:57 avg 0.21, max 0.28) and jumps to avg 60.29 / max 60.8 in the 15:00:00Z bucket, staying 58.9-66.4% thereafter. Change dep-6203 (v6.0.0) deployed 14:46:00Z, so the lag from deploy to onset is ~14 min (consistent with the reported '~15 min after release'), but onset does NOT coincide with the deploy.

Non-mandate writers to the shared ledger-db fail simultaneously with disk-space errors: order-service (no MANDATE_HOLD path) emits 236 ERROR lines, single pattern 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device orderId=<n>', first at 2026-06-01T15:00:42Z, last 16:57:47Z. This failure is generic, not entry-type specific.

payment-service's own error signature is identical in kind: 354 ERROR lines, all one pattern 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device (payment <n>)', first 2026-06-01T15:00:26Z. The message names no entry type (no MANDATE_HOLD vs legacy distinction), so it does not localize the failure to the new mandate path.

The onset order across components matches a shared-datastore disk exhaustion, not an app-path defect: payment-service first error 15:00:26Z, order-service first error 15:00:42Z (~16s later), and per T1's finding ledger-db first PANIC at 15:01:01Z. All three are the same 'No space left on device' signature within ~35s.

Blast radius extends to every service writing to ledger-db except payment/order in this window: portfolio-service and settlement-service returned 0 ERROR lines for 14:30-16:59Z (total_matched 0, not truncated), and api-gateway returned 0 ERROR lines — so the failure is datastore-wide but only visible in the two writers that had matching traffic/log capture.

events.description: Could not retrieve payment-service INFO-level logs to count successes/failures split by ledger entry type (searches for 'ledger entry', 'mandate', 'PAYMENT' all returned total_matched 0 — these may be wrong contains strings or the level filter excluded them).
No ledger-db disk_used_pct / slow_queries_per_min timeline was retrieved (metric names confirmed available per T1's F12, but budget ran out before querying the values).
portfolio-service and settlement-service returned zero ERROR logs, but there is no independent confirmation they had write traffic in this window (no request-rate metric checked for them).

events.answer: Error onset is 15:00Z (between the 14:57Z and 15:00Z buckets), ~14 min after the 14:46Z v6.0.0 deploy — so the '~15 min after release' lag is right but the theory that the release caused it is not supported. Errors are NOT confined to the new mandate-flow/ledger entry type: order-service, which has no MANDATE_HOLD path, fails with the same 'No space left on device' signature starting 15:00:42Z, only ~16s after payment-service's first error at 15:00:26Z. This rules out the release-introduced entry type as the sole cause; the failures are a shared ledger-db disk-full condition affecting all writers.

ledger-db infrastructure/disk failure (node or volume degraded) rather than runaway write growth
